newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: SOCCER-RUFER DOUBLE HELPS NEW ZEALAND CRUSH FIJI.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUFER DOUBLE HELPS NEW ZEALAND CRUSH FIJI.

text.p: Two goals by veteran striker Wynton Rufer helped New Zealand crush Fiji 5-0 in a World Cup qualifier on Wednesday and book a showdown with Australia to decide Oceania's representatives for the concluding battle for a place in the finals in France next year.
Rufer, 34, scored a goal in each half of a one-sided match before leaving the pitch with nine minutes remaining.

The Fijians, who were no match for a much better organised New Zealand side, were reduced to 10 men in the 56th minute when midfielder Jope Lomu was sent off for punching New Zealand striker Tim Stevens.
The win guaranteed New Zealand top place in their qualifying group and set up a two-leg play-off with Australia, with the first leg scheduled for Auckland on June 28.
The Australians built an unassailable lead in their group by thrashing the Solomon Islands 6-2 on Tuesday.
The winners of the Australia-New Zealand encounter face a play-off against the fourth-placed team in the Asian preliminary competition for a berth in the World Cup finals.
